youtube.title: The day is shrinking fast
youtube.caption:
The day falls from 24 hours to 12 and the ground at the equator speeds up to 3,340 km/h.

Part 2 of 8 of "What If Earth Spun Faster and Couldn't Stop?" — the full video is on this channel.

Sources
1. Speed of the ground at the equator: 1,674 km/h today, 3,340 km/h at a 12 h day, 6,679 km/h at 6 h, 13,358 km/h at 3 h, 20,038 km/h at 2 h and 26,717 km/h at 1.5 h. The Sun is up for half of each day. (our calculation; the arithmetic is shown in the film)
2. The Sun's apparent motion is 360° divided by the day length: 0.5° per minute at a 12 h day, 2° per minute at 3 h and 4° per minute at 1.5 h. The Sun's disk is about 0.53° wide, so it moves its own width every 64 s, 16 s and 8 s. — NASA Science, Sun Facts (angular size about 0.53 degrees): https://science.nasa.gov/sun/facts/
3. The ground at the equator moves at about 1,674 km/h (465 m/s): one trip around the equator divided by the length of a day. That is about 1/17 of the speed needed to orbit. (our calculation; the arithmetic is shown in the film)
4. The speed of sound in air at sea level is about 340 m/s. The equator moves at 2.7 times that at a 12 h day (929 m/s) and 1.35 times at 6 h (463 m/s). — NASA Glenn, Speed of sound: https://www.grc.nasa.gov/www/k-12/airplane/sound.html
5. Your weight as a share of what it would be on a non-spinning Earth: 99.7% today, 98.6% at a 12 h day, 94.5% at 6 h, 78.0% at 3 h, 50.4% at 2 h and 11.9% at 1.5 h. A 70 kg person weighs 69 kg at 12 h and 55 kg at 3 h. (our calculation; the arithmetic is shown in the film)

Narration: synthetic voice (AI). Thumbnail illustration made with AI. Animation: code-rendered, no stock footage. Every number is checked against the sources.

Possibility Lab: Impossible questions, honest assumptions, real calculations.
